claims.finding: Korn Ferry closed an acquisition eight days before this print and paid for at least part of it in newly issued unregistered stock: 8-K 2026-06-29 items 1.01/3.02/7.01/9.01 (signing plus an unregistered equity issuance), 8-K 2026-08-19 items 1.01/2.03/8.01/9.01 (a new direct financial obligation, i.e. deal financing), 8-K 2026-09-01 items 2.01/3.02/7.01/9.01 (completion plus a second unregistered equity issuance) - and Item 3.02 is only reportable above 1% of shares outstanding, so each of those two issuances was at least ~530k shares, roughly $44m of stock at the current price.

claims.why_not_priced: Korn Ferry guides diluted EPS a quarter at a time, and event.json records consensus at $1.35 - exactly the midpoint of the $1.32-$1.38 range the company itself set on 2026-06-23, before the deal was even signed. The consensus therefore contains no deal at all, while the guide the company must issue at this print covers a quarter (August-October) that is two thirds post-close and carries first-time intangible amortisation, interest on the August 19 obligation and at least 1% more shares. What is priced is the fact of the deal, which was a Reg FD (item 7.01) release; what is not priced is the shape of the guide, because nobody outside the company has the target's financials. If the guide mechanics were already in the numbers, consensus would not still sit on the pre-deal midpoint.
claims.independence: The tape from a different source in the capture points the same way: quote.json has KFY closing at 85.55 on 2026-08-31, its high for the series, and the baseline then records spot 82.04 on 2026-09-08 with run_up_5d_pct of -4.10 - the entire drawdown falls in the five sessions that begin the day the closing 8-K was accepted (2026-09-01 20:38 UTC). The financing leg is a separate document: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/56679/000119312526357084/d417124d8k.htm

claims.finding: Korn Ferry's beat over consensus has been decaying quarter by quarter - adjusted EPS $1.31 vs $1.24 (+5.6%) on 2025-09-09, $1.28 vs $1.23 (+4.1%) on 2026-03-09, $1.40 vs $1.38 (+1.4%) on 2026-06-23 - so the +5.83%, +4.00%, +6.46% and +7.60% up-reactions the baseline is built from were earned in a fat-beat regime that has already halved twice.

claims.why_not_priced: The three data points sit in three separate messages nine months apart inside one social dump; the sell-side preview line is 'beaten in N consecutive quarters', which is directionally the opposite reading of the same facts. The decay also explains something the baseline cannot: why the 2026-03-09 print, on a $0.05 beat, still went -1.53%. If the market had marked the beat regime down, consensus would sit below the guide midpoint rather than exactly on it, and the name would not have been within 4.9% of its 52-week high a week before the print.
claims.independence: Same source cluster as nothing else here - this rests only on docs/f52fae6941a874956cc2c58ea2ab58deffdc2526.txt, which is a different document from finding 1's filings.json evidence.
